title: Normalized ringed restriction exchange and open descent
statement:
Let $p:P\to T$ and $h:T'\to T$ be morphisms of schemes, let $P'=P\times_TT'$ with projections $h':P'\to P$ and $p':P'\to T'$ [def-pc-scheme; def-pc-fibre-product], and let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$. Use small site representatives in a common larger universe [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site; def-weil-size-convention]. On $P,T',P'$ use respectively $p^{-1}R,h^{-1}R,h'^{-1}p^{-1}R\cong p'^{-1}h^{-1}R$. Module inverse image is the exact topos inverse image with its transported action and without extension of scalars [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image; def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories and total right derived direct images [def-weil-abstract-derived-category; def-sfb-right-derived-functor].

For a complex $K$ of $p^{-1}R$-module sheaves, let $\operatorname{bc}_K:h^{-1}p_*K\to p'_*h'^{-1}K$ be formed termwise as the adjunct of $p'^{-1}h^{-1}p_*K\cong h'^{-1}p^{-1}p_*K\to h'^{-1}K$, with the last arrow the counit. Choose K-injective resolutions $a:K\to I$ and $b:h'^{-1}I\to J$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. The class of
$$h^{-1}p_*I\xrightarrow{\operatorname{bc}_I}p'_*h'^{-1}I\xrightarrow{p'_*b}p'_*J$$
defines a natural morphism $\operatorname{Ex}_{h,p,K}:h^{-1}Rp_*K\to Rp'_*h'^{-1}K$, independent of the choices under their canonical derived comparisons. It is the derived counit mate of the canonical pullback-square comparison, for the derived adjunctions $u^{-1}\dashv Ru_*$ ($u=p,p'$) obtained by deriving the ordinary module adjunctions, i.e. those for which the Hom transpose of the class of every chain map $u^{-1}L\to I$ into a K-injective complex $I$ is the class of its ordinary transpose $L\to u_*I$. For a module $M$, writing $\delta_{p,M}:(p_*M)[0]\to Rp_*(M[0])$ for the canonical comparison, it satisfies
$$\operatorname{Ex}_{h,p,M[0]}\circ h^{-1}\delta_{p,M}=\delta_{p',h'^{-1}M}\circ\operatorname{bc}_M[0].$$

For an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow T$, let $j_P:P_U\hookrightarrow P$, $j':T'_U\hookrightarrow T'$, $j_{P'}:P'_U\hookrightarrow P'$ be its base changes and $p_U,h_U,p'_U,h'_U$ the restricted square. For every scheme map $f:S\to Z$, sheaf of rings $R_Z$ and open $V\hookrightarrow Z$, there is an isomorphism $j_V^{-1}Rf_*\cong Rf_{V,*}j_S^{-1}$ over the actual inverse-image rings, represented on a K-injective $I$ by the section identification $I(S\times_Z Q)=I(S_V\times_V Q)$ for $Q\to V$. Through these open comparisons and the canonical inverse-image composition maps, one has equality of derived morphisms
$$j'^{-1}\operatorname{Ex}_{h,p,K}=\operatorname{Ex}_{h_U,p_U,j_P^{-1}K}.$$
For every small open cover $T=\bigcup_aU_a$, $\operatorname{Ex}_{h,p,K}$ is invertible if all its restricted exchanges on $T'\times_TU_a$ are invertible. The exchange for an identity $h$ is the identity under resolution comparisons; empty schemes and zero complexes are included. These assertions require no separatedness, finite type, properness or constructibility assumptions.

proof.text: Use the geometric inverse image of [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor] for each scheme map. The forgetful functor in [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] is faithful and exact and computes kernels and cokernels on underlying abelian sheaves. Thus inverse image with its transported action is additive and exact: its underlying functor is the exact abelian inverse image, and a sequence of module sheaves is exact precisely when its underlying sequence is. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] with the structural ring map the identity of the inverse-image ring; tensoring over that ring with itself is the identity, giving the specified ordinary adjunction. The inverse-image composition isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition] respect these actions: apply their naturality to the action map and their finite-product comparisons. On the Cartesian square they give $c:p'^{-1}h^{-1}\cong h'^{-1}p^{-1}$, with the corresponding identification of coefficient rings. Lean coefficient coherence: define the canonical inverse-image compositor with an explicitly specified equal composite scheme map. Conjugation sends it to the corresponding direct-image compositor. The site square is the inverse first compositor followed by the second compositor with the same chosen composite; this follows by substitution in pullbackComp. Since sheaf pushforward transports natural isomorphisms functorially, conjugateIsoEquiv injectivity identifies ringSquareIso with the inverse first ring compositor followed by the second. Evaluating its inverse at R cancels the second compositor, giving actualCoefficients_coherent. HEq transports the original composite maps to the common chosen map, without changing any coefficient isomorphism.

For transpose_normalization, use the existing exact-left/right-derived adjunction. On homotopy categories its unit satisfies Adjunction.derivedη_fac_app. Expanding homEquiv_unit and applying naturality of the right-derived unit gives the ordinary homotopy transpose followed by that unit. On quotient objects, the degreewise adjunction unit is the quotient of the chain adjunction unit. Transport along quotientCompQhIso and the explicit inverse of rightDerivedFunctorObjQIso proves precisely the stated chain-map transpose normalization. K-injective resolutions and the derived adjunction exist by the recorded dependencies. This replaces the proposed proof through two Hom-set bijections; it proves the actual chosen adjunction has the required normalization.

proof.text:
For $f:S\to Z$ and $V\hookrightarrow Z$, [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-comparison] identifies actual inverse-image module restriction with slice restriction. By [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized-universes], a K-injective $I$ on $S$ restricts to a K-injective $j_S^{-1}I$ on $S_V$. Apply [lem-sfb-proetale-open-restriction-counit] termwise to obtain
$$j_V^{-1}f_*I\cong f_{V,*}j_S^{-1}I.$$
The right side computes $Rf_{V,*}j_S^{-1}K$ and the left computes $j_V^{-1}Rf_*K$. The displayed isomorphism on an object $Q\to V$ is precisely $I(S\times_ZQ)=I(S_V\times_VQ)$, with identical actions after the inverse-image ring identification. Naturality of this ordinary isomorphism and the canonical homotopy comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] show it descends naturally and independently of $I$. Its counit equation descends too, since it is an equality of chain maps before localization. Lean implementation of K-injective preservation: use the ringed open comparison to identify inverse image with overFunctor followed by the inverse site equivalence. The localized restriction theorem gives K-injective preservation for overFunctor. ScalarExtensionRingIso identifies actual changeOfRings along c with restriction along c.inv; this is the inverse of the scalar equivalence. Equivalences preserve K-injectives, and preservation is stable under composition and natural isomorphism. The chosen Cartesian-square hom_fst makes the upper horizontal map an open immersion, so the same theorem applies there. For open_representative, specialize resolution_formula to a=id and b=id and cancel the two canonical comparison isomorphisms. The preservation argument is now factored into the fully proved functor-level instances [lem-sf-proetale-open-pullback-preserves-kinjective] and [lem-sf-upper-open-pullback-preserves-kinjective]. The existing complex-level theorem signatures remain, and the generic map-complex instance supplies the same inference from these preservation instances. Cancellation in open_representative is performed by a generic two-isomorphism cancellation lemma before specializing to module-sheaf derived categories. The ordinary geometric assertion is factored into [lem-sf-ringed-ordinary-open-exchange]. For open_comparison, apply exchange_chainUnit on a K-injective I. Both cochain units are inverse right-derived object comparisons, since upper open pullback preserves K-injectives. The ordinary exchange is an isomorphism degreewise, so its chain map and its image under Q are isomorphisms. The chain-unit equation and cancellation show exchange at QI invertible. Resolve a representative of an arbitrary derived object K and transport invertibility along QI isomorphic to K by naturality. This proves the entire derived half from the ordinary geometric assertion, without a new derived comparison or choice of a natural inverse. For open_sectionwise, use the existing proEtaleOpenRestrictionCounit to obtain beta with its Sectionwise formula and an alpha with AlphaNormalization and CounitEquation. Apply lem-sf-ringed-open-square-unit-normalization to the inverse of the selected actual-ring module square. The two alphas have equal transposes under the composite ordinary adjunction: their sectionwise unit normalizations are identical. Injectivity of homEquiv therefore identifies alpha with the inverse selected square. Apply injectivity of the target ordinary adjunction transpose to beta and ordinary(actualSquare), cancel alpha, and use CounitEquation and mateEquiv_counit. This proves equality of the natural transformations, while retaining the existing Sectionwise formula unchanged.

proof.text: Apply restriction_exchange_cube to the specified OpenCube. This proved derived-cube helper localizes the ordinary inverse-image cube, identifies the six canonical comparisons, and takes the four exchange mates. Unfolding the pullSquare abbreviation gives exactly the open_restriction equation; its openness hypothesis is not needed for this equality.

The Cartesian base faces identify each local base open with the pullback of the covering open of Y. The pullback range formula and the chosen Cartesian isomorphisms show these opens cover Y prime. For every a, open_comparison makes exchange of the source and target open faces invertible. The pullSquare maps are isomorphisms, and localIso makes the remaining local exchange invertible. Rewrite open_restriction and cancel the invertible target-face exchange and upper pullSquare comparison: native restriction of the global exchange to each local base open is invertible. Apply [lem-sf-proetale-ringed-open-cover-reflects-iso] with the coefficient rings and isomorphisms stored in OpenCube. This proves open_descent for arbitrary complexes, including empty covers, without separately constructing derived models of all slice categories.

proof.text: When $h=1_T$, identify the square with the identity square and choose $J=I$, $b=1$. The ordinary exchange is $1_{p_*I}$: its transpose is the counit, which is also the transpose of the identity by the adjunction triangle. The formula of step 3 is therefore the identity, and step 4 handles arbitrary resolution choices. For the zero complex choose the zero resolution. The empty-site module categories are zero categories (the empty covering forces the unique section), so all formulas and the empty-cover case hold there as well. No step has used separatedness, finite type, properness, constructibility, boundedness or a constant coefficient ring. identityDirect_existsUnique is constructed directly by SheafOfModules.pushforwardCongr₂ along the inverse of pullbackId, followed by pushforwardId. The unit equation for the adjunction-conjugate coefficient ringId identifies its structural map with the canonical direct-image identity. The construction has the required section formula definitionally. Equality on all module sections proves uniqueness. For identityCoefficients_coherent, conjugate the generalized compositors for id followed by p and p followed by id. The unit laws for pullbackComp and the adjunction conjugation laws identify these with the left and right unitors followed by the canonical inverse-image identity comparisons. Evaluate at the ring sheaf. Naturality of the identity comparison moves the given coefficient map c through the left expression; cancellation of each identity comparison with its inverse makes both expressions equal to c. HEq again transports to the common composite p. The remaining identity exchange normalization retains the preceding plan.
